claim: New WHOOP apps start on a Sandbox tier of 10 members.
quote: Every new app starts on the Sandbox tier, which allows up to 10 WHOOP members to connect.

claim: The tiers run 10, 100, 1,000, 5,000 and unlimited.
quote: Sandbox 10 Build 100 Growth 1,000 Scale 5,000 Production Unlimited

claim: Tiers are requested one at a time; from Build onward half the current limit must be connected.
quote: Tiers are earned one at a time. You can only request the tier directly above your current one. From Build onward, moving up requires at least 50% of your current tier's member limit to be connected.

claim: Each request is reviewed by hand.
quote: Requests are reviewed manually, in the order they are received.

claim: Each request needs testing with at least one real member.
quote: Ensure that you have tested your app with at least one WHOOP member.

claim: Each request needs complete app details.
quote: In particular, make sure your App Name , Contact Email(s) , and Privacy Policy URL are filled in and accurate to accelerate the review.

claim: Each request needs adherence to WHOOP's brand guidelines.
quote: Verify your app adheres to the WHOOP Design and Brand Guidelines .

claim: Fitbit / Garmin and table: Garmin's developer program needs Garmin's approval.
quote: After you request access to the Garmin Connect Developer Program and your request has been approved, you will be granted access to the Garmin Developer Portal and can get started on your integration right away.

claim: Fitbit / Garmin: now as Starter and Enterprise Access.
quote: Starter Access: Developers can gain immediate access and launch with Garmin, with access to core data and tools.

claim: Fitbit / Garmin: now as Starter and Enterprise Access.
quote: Enterprise Access: For companies operating at scale, this new model aligns with growth, offering expanded data access, reliability, and enterprise-grade support.

claim: Fitbit / Garmin and table: some features are marked Supported with Enterprise Access only.
quote: Supported with Enterprise Access only

claim: WHOOP says you need a WHOOP membership to develop an app.
quote: You must have a WHOOP membership to develop an app on the Developer Platform.

claim: The API requests consent from WHOOP members.
quote: you can use the OAuth standard to request consent from WHOOP members to access data on their behalf.

claim: Oura: its own 10-user cap until Oura approves your app.
quote: By default, API Applications have a ten user limit.

claim: Terra's docs say 150+ integrations.
quote: Click Add New and choose from 150+ integrations.

claim: Terra: WHOOP connects through your own app on the WHOOP developer portal.
quote: WHOOP requires every company to connect users through its own app on the WHOOP developer portal

claim: Terra's integrations page says Google turned the Fitbit Web API off on 2 November 2026.
quote: Google turned off the Fitbit Web API on 2 November 2026

claim: Rook: over 400 health data sources and wearable devices.
quote: The integration ecosystem consolidates access to over 400 health data sources and wearable devices.

claim: Rook: clients create their own WHOOP developer account.
quote: clients are required to create their own developer accounts with these providers.

claim: Junction's docs say 300+ devices.
quote: Connect to 300+ devices, and receive data in Junction standardized schemas.

claim: Junction supports WHOOP with Bring Your Own OAuth.
quote: WHOOP BYOO is available for the Launch, Grow and Scale plans

claim: Junction was formerly Vital.
quote: Vital was always about helping healthcare systems operate more effectively.

claim: Terra from $499 a month billed monthly.
quote: Subscriptions start from $399 per month billed annually, or $499 per month billed monthly.

claim: Junction $300 a month for up to 500 connected users.
quote: Launch covers 1-500 connected users.

claim: Junction $300 a month for up to 500 connected users.
quote: for a flat $300 a month

claim: Rook from $399 a month for up to 750 active users.
quote: $399 USD per month Up to 750 active users

claim: Google lists November 2, 2026 as the Fitbit Web API and Fitbit OAuth turn-off.
quote: The Fitbit Web API and Fitbit OAuth endpoints will be turned off and will no longer function or sync data to or from Fitbit users.

claim: Google tells developers to migrate applications and users to the Google Health API and Google OAuth 2.0.
quote: must migrate their applications and users to the Google Health API and Google OAuth 2.0

claim: The Google Health API returns data from Fitbit devices and Pixel watches.
quote: All Fitbit devices and Google Pixel watches, current and previous, will collect data that is returned through the Google Health API.
